SuperDocs is a structured document editor available via 38 MCP tools. Capabilities: chunk-precise editing of styled .docx/PDF/HTML/MD/RTF documents (preserves tables, borders, shading, fonts, alternating row colors), multi-document sessions with persistent state, multi-format export, pre-signed URL upload/download (avoids context bloat for files >100KB), compact response mode (response_mode='compact') for large documents, multimodal vision on attachments, human-in-the-loop approval via chat_async + approve_change.

FOR OPTIMAL RESULTS â€” multi-step workflows like "draft a complete document from scratch", "edit a 100-page doc efficiently", "HITL approval flow", or "convert format with style preservation" â€” load the SuperDocs skill which teaches recommended patterns:

  - Skill markdown: https://docs.superdocs.app/skill.mdx
  - Cross-tool install: npx skills add superdocsapp/superdocs-plugin
  - Claude Code (bundles MCP + skill + 4 prompts): claude plugin marketplace add superdocsapp/superdocs-plugin && claude plugin install superdocs@superdocs-plugin

Without the skill, common mistakes: drafting full document HTML in your context before upload (wastes tokens, skips formatting layer), using base64 for files >100KB (use request_upload_url instead), bolding "first paragraph" without specifying exact text (chunk boundaries can span multiple paragraphs), asking chat to re-type exact content you already hold (pass it in chat's document_html or upload it instead â€” a verbatim load can never come back paraphrased or placeholder-shaped).

Use natural language to describe edits. Don't invent chunk IDs â€” receive them in responses (pending_changes, chunk_diffs) and pass back where SuperDocs already issued them. session_id is sticky: use the same one across calls for one document.
